summary:
AFTER LIFTOFF is an interactive digital archive that tells the stories of space machines left behind on the Moon and Mars. It was created in response to NASA's challenge, "Abandoned but not Forgotten."

The project focuses on making space history easier and more interesting to explore, especially for students aged 10 to 16. Visitors can explore two destinations, the Moon and Mars, and learn about real machines such as the Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage and the Sojourner rover.

Through visual content, mission information, and interactive sections, the website explains why these machines were sent, what they did, and what happened after their missions.

AFTER LIFTOFF aims to make scientific information more accessible and help young people understand the technology, discoveries, and history behind space exploration.
details:
AFTER LIFTOFF is an interactive educational website created to share the stories of space machines left on the Moon and Mars.

The website is organized into two main destinations: the Moon and Mars. Visitors can choose where they want to explore and discover information about real space missions and their equipment.

The project presents machines such as the Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage and the Sojourner rover. Each story explains the machine's purpose, its role in the mission, its achievements, and what happened after the mission ended.

The website uses visual elements, accessible text, mission information, and interactive sections to make learning easier and more interesting. It is designed mainly for students aged 10 to 16, but it can also be used by teachers, families, and people interested in space exploration.

Our creative approach is to present these machines as important parts of space history instead of treating them as forgotten objects. We connect their engineering and missions with the scientific knowledge they helped create.

We used Base44 to develop the website and digital tools to organize and present the information. NASA mission resources were used to support the historical and scientific content.

AFTER LIFTOFF could be used in schools, science clubs, libraries, and STEM activities. Its digital format makes it easy to share and could help more students, including those in the Dominican Republic, learn about space science.

Our goal is to make space history more accessible and show that the end of a mission does not mean the end of its contribution to science.
